terms.definition: A pre-configured template containing the operating system, applications, files, and configuration settings needed to launch EC2 instances
terms.example: Like a master recipe that lets you create identical servers - one AMI can launch 1 instance or 1000 instances with the same configuration

terms.definition: AWS's Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) offering that provides resizable virtual servers in the cloud
terms.example: Like renting a computer in the cloud - you can choose the size, turn it on/off, and pay only for what you use

terms.definition: A running virtual server created from an AMI template
terms.example: If AMI is a house blueprint, an instance is the actual house built from that blueprint

terms.definition: AMIs created and maintained by AWS with the highest trust level and regular security updates
terms.example: Amazon Linux 2023, Ubuntu Server, Windows Server - all verified and supported by AWS or official vendors

terms.definition: AMIs created by you from your own configured EC2 instances, private to your AWS account
terms.example: You configure one perfect web server, save it as 'WebServer-v1.0', then launch 50 identical servers from it

terms.definition: Publicly shared AMIs created by AWS users without any verification from AWS
terms.example: Like downloading software from random people on the internet - may contain malware, never use for production

terms.definition: The core of the Linux operating system that manages hardware resources including CPU, memory, and devices
terms.example: Like the engine management system in a car - it controls all the parts and makes sure everything runs smoothly

terms.definition: A command-line interface that interprets user commands and communicates with the operating system
terms.example: Like a translator between you and the computer - you type commands in human-readable text, shell converts to system operations

terms.definition: A text-based interface where users type commands to interact with the operating system
terms.example: Instead of clicking buttons, you type 'ls' to list files, 'cd' to change directories - powerful for automation

terms.definition: A visual interface with windows, icons, and buttons for interacting with computers
terms.example: Windows Explorer, macOS Finder - you click and drag instead of typing commands

terms.definition: A protocol for secure remote access to Linux/Unix servers, uses port 22
terms.example: Like a secure phone call to your server - you log in remotely and control it via command line

terms.definition: A set of cryptographic keys (public and private) used for SSH authentication to EC2 instances
terms.example: Public key is like a padlock on your server, private key (.pem file) is the key only you have - lose the key, lose access forever

terms.definition: A virtual firewall that controls inbound and outbound traffic to EC2 instances
terms.example: Like a security guard checking ID - allows SSH from your IP, allows HTTPS from anywhere, blocks everything else

terms.definition: The hardware specification for an EC2 instance including CPU, RAM, network, and storage performance
terms.example: t3.micro (1 vCPU, 1GB RAM) for testing, m5.large (2 vCPU, 8GB RAM) for production - like choosing laptop specs

terms.definition: Persistent block storage volumes that can be attached to EC2 instances
terms.example: Like an external hard drive that persists even when you turn off the computer - data survives instance stops

terms.definition: A geographical area containing multiple isolated data centers (Availability Zones)
terms.example: us-east-1 (Virginia), eu-west-1 (Ireland) - AMIs created in one region only exist in that region

terms.definition: An EC2 instance that is powered off but preserves all configuration and EBS data
terms.example: Like hibernating your laptop - turns off to save power (money), but everything is saved for when you start it again

terms.definition: An EC2 instance that is powered on and fully operational
terms.example: Like a laptop that's turned on and working - you pay full price per hour for compute, memory, and network

terms.definition: An EC2 instance that has been permanently deleted
terms.example: Like throwing away a computer - it's gone forever (unless you configured EBS volumes to persist)

terms.definition: A firewall that tracks connection states and automatically allows response traffic
terms.example: Security Groups are stateful - if you allow inbound SSH, outbound responses are automatically allowed without separate rules

terms.definition: A collection of free software tools and utilities that work with the Linux kernel
terms.example: Commands like ls, grep, tar, bash - these aren't part of the kernel, they're GNU tools that make Linux usable

terms.definition: Software that installs, updates, and removes applications on Linux systems
terms.example: apt on Ubuntu (apt install nginx), yum on Amazon Linux (yum install httpd) - like an app store for servers

terms.definition: A complete Linux operating system package combining the kernel with specific tools and configurations
terms.example: Ubuntu, Amazon Linux 2023, Red Hat - all use the Linux kernel but package different tools and support

terms.definition: Cloud service model providing virtualized computing resources over the internet
terms.example: EC2 is IaaS - you get virtual servers but manage the OS and applications yourself

terms.definition: Infrastructure pattern where servers are never modified after deployment - changes create new instances
terms.example: Don't update running servers, create new AMI with updates and deploy fresh instances - enables instant rollback
